message.reasoning_content:
The user wants a block-breaker (Breakout/Arkanoid) game. Language: Japanese. Let me build a complete single-file HTML game — a polished, crafted Breakout with: - Canvas-based game with real physics - Multiple levels with distinct block layouts - Power-ups (multi-ball, wide paddle, laser, slow ball, extra life) - Particle effects, screen shake, block shatter - Distinctive typography display face + readable body face. For Japanese, Google Fonts via "Font Family", with a condensed/heavy display for scores/titles — "Bungee" reads like arcade signage and has a strong personality, pairing well with "Zen Kaku Gothic New" for body. The fun pairing: display for titles/score, body for Japanese copy. Palette: the obvious move for a block-breaker is a near-black background with a single neon accent — but that's exactly the well-worn look I want to sidestep. Better to make it feel distinctive: a "vintage arcade CRT" with a rich deep-teal/plum base and a warm multi-color block palette. Or an "Orbit" style. Let me do: a deep midnight-indigo-blue panel for the playfield, but the page shell is a warm off-white/paper with arcade cabinet chrome — that's a strong distinctive direction. The page is a bright coral-amber arcade cabinet against a dark ink backdrop — a chunky arcade cabinet on a warm speckled background, with the playfield itself a deep space-blue. That gives strong contrast without leaning on either the cream-and-serif look or the single-neon-on-black look. Colors: - Page bg: #12141c deep ink with layered ambient (scanlines, subtle grid, drifting glow). - Cabinet: solid deep magenta-red block with thick borders and chunky offset shadows — bold arcade look. Let me lean into a "1978 arcade console" look: bold blocky panels, chunky borders, offset hard shadows, saturated primaries (vermilion #FF4B2B, amber #FFC43D, teal #12B0A0, deep navy #10192B, bone #F2EFE6). Typography: "Bungee" for display (arcade signage) + "Zen Kaku Gothic New" for body. For Japanese body text, need a Japanese font. "Zen Kaku Gothic New" is a good bold-weight-capable Japanese sans. Display: Bungee is Latin only, so for Japanese headings I need a Japanese display face. "Zen Kaku Gothic New" 900 is heavy and works for Japanese display. Bungee for Latin/numbers (score). Good. Game features: - Canvas with devicePixelRatio scaling - Paddle controlled by mouse/touch/keyboard (← →) - Ball with substepping to prevent tunneling - Brick types: normal (1 hit), tough (2-3 hits with visual cracks), steel (unbreakable), explosive (chain reaction) - Power-ups falling: multiball, expand, laser, slow, life, sticky? - Levels: 5 designed layouts, then procedural - Score, combo multiplier, lives, level indicator - Screen shake, particles, brick flash, trail on ball - Sound with WebAudio (blips), mute toggle - Start screen, pause, level clear banner, game over, victory - HUD rendered in DOM (HTML overlay) for crisp typography, side panel with stats, power-up legend - High score in localStorage - Keyboard shortcuts Layout: an asymmetric composition — left rail with vertical branding, the game stage as a chunky panel, and a right rail with HUD (score, level, lives, powerup log, controls). On mobile: stack. I'll build the HUD in DOM for crisp text, and the playfield in canvas. Add a CRT scanline overlay and vignette on the canvas. Let me write the code carefully. Canvas logical size: 720 x 900? Classic breakout is portrait. Let's do logical 640x800 and scale down via CSS to fit. Actually with side panels, the playfield at ~560x720 fits typical laptop. Use responsive scaling: canvas CSS width fits container, internal resolution scaled. Physics details: - Ball radius 8, base speed ~ 380 px/s increasing with level & paddle hits. - Substeps: divide movement into steps of max 4px. - Paddle collision: reflect angle based on offset from center: angle = offset * 60deg. - Brick collision: AABB vs circle; determine side by penetration depth. Bricks grid: cols 11, cell width ~ 52. Playfield width 640 with wall margin 16. cols = 10, brick width ~57, gap 4. Let's compute: playW=640, margin 20 each side => 600. cols=10 => cell 60, brick w=54, gap 6, h=22, gap 6. Level designs: patterns defined as string rows with chars: - '.' empty - '1','2','3' hit points colors - 'S' steel - 'X' explosive - 'C' color index? Simpler: digits = hp, color derived from row. Let me define palette per hp: 1=teal, 2=amber, 3=vermilion, plus special: steel = slate, explosive = magenta with pulsing glow. Power-ups: - M: multiball (3 balls) - W: widen paddle - L: laser (shoot with space, 5s? give 12 shots) - S: slow ball - +: extra life - G: gravity? keep it simple: 5 types. Falling powerup catch with paddle. Lasers: paddle shoots two bullets upward. Scoring: brick base 50 * hp, combo multiplier increments per brick without paddle touch, resets on paddle hit. Display combo prominently when >1. Level clear: bonus = remaining lives * 500 + time bonus. Then next level. Lives: 3. Losing a life: screen flash, shake, reset ball on paddle (sticky start: ball attached to paddle, click/space to launch). Game over / victory screens with stats and restart. Also add "PAUSE" with P/Esc. Let's also add a small "powerup log" in the right rail that shows recently collected items with a flash animation, and a level progress bar (bricks remaining). Ambient background: layered radial gradients + animated drifting "brick" shapes (CSS animation), plus subtle grain. Keep tasteful. Micro-interactions: buttons with hard offset shadow that shift on hover/active; score digits with a "tick" animation; lives as small ball icons that pop when lost; hover tooltips on powerup legend. Scroll reveals: the page is mostly one screen; but add a section below with "攻略ガイド" (power-up legend + tips). Scroll reveal for those. Let me write it. HTML structure: ```
...
logo + tagline + score chip
vertical text, level, lives
start/pause/gameover screens
buttons
score, combo, powerups log, progress
powerup cards + tips
``` The opening should feel like the machine itself rather than a plain title: masthead as an arcade marquee with the game title, coin-slot detail, high score. Then immediately the playfield. Let me write CSS with custom properties. Palette: --ink: #0B0E17 (page bg deep) --panel: #131829 --bone: #F3EEE3 --vermilion: #FF4A2E --amber: #FFC33D --teal: #17C3AE --blue: #2E6BE6? maybe --sky: #4EA8DE --magenta: #F0408C? avoid overuse. --steel: #46536E Cabinet: bone panel with thick ink border, offset shadow in vermilion. Actually a bone-colored cabinet on dark bg gives strong contrast — good. Canvas background: deep navy gradient with faint grid, plus a "floor" line. Now write JS. Constants: ``` const W=640,H=840; wall top area: HUD is in DOM so canvas top margin 24. ``` Let me set canvas logical 640 x 820. Walls: left/right 14, top 14, bottom = open (lose). Paddle: y = H-56, w=104, h=14, r=7. Ball r=7. Brick area: top=90, left=20, cols=10, cellW=(640-40)/10=60, brickW=54, brickH=22, gapX=6, gapY=7. Level definitions: array of {name, rows:[strings], ballSpeed}. 10 chars per row. Level 1: 6 rows full of '1's. Level 2: pyramid with '2's. Level 3: checker + steel. Level 4: with explosives and steel core. Level 5: dense, hp 3 on top. Then endless procedural (levels beyond 5) generated with patterns. Brick colors by hp: 1 -> teal, 2 -> amber, 3 -> vermilion, steel -> slate, explosive -> magenta with pulsing glow. Draw bricks as rounded rects with inner highlight line, cracks overlay for damaged bricks. Collision: iterate bricks near ball (small array, just loop all; ≤110 bricks fine). Circle-AABB resolution: compute closest point; if distance < r then collide. Determine normal from penetration: compute overlap along x and y using previous position; simpler: use ball center vs brick rect: ``` const cx=clamp(b.x, br.x, br.x+br.w), cy=clamp(b.y, br.y, br.y+br.h); const dx=b.x-cx, dy=b.y-cy; if(dx*dx+dy*dy < r*r) { // resolve: if ball center inside rect horizontally & vertically... // use normal from (dx,dy) if not zero, else from penetration } ``` Standard approach: if |dx| > |dy| reflect vx, else reflect vy; push ball out. Handle the case where dx==0 && dy==0 (center inside): push out using min penetration. Substepping: compute steps = ceil(speed*dt / 4). Particles: on brick break spawn 8-14 squares with velocity, gravity, fade. Sparks ring for explosive. Screen shake: shakeMag decays. Sound: WebAudio simple oscillator blips. Function beep(freq, dur, type, gain). Brick hit: square wave with freq scaled by row. Launch, paddle: triangle. Powerup: arpeggio. Lose: descending. Also add subtle ambient? No, keep SFX. Lives as ball icons. Powerup drop chance 0.14, weighted. Laser: while active (8s), space fires; bullets 3px x 12px, speed 600 up, destroy bricks. Multiball: spawn 2 extra balls from existing ball with angle spread. Slow: multiply all ball speeds by 0.65 for 8s (store factor and restore). Widen: paddle target width 160 for 10s. Life: +1 life (max 6). Also "sticky"? skip. Level progress bar: destroyed/total. Combo: consecutive brick hits without touching paddle. Multiplier = 1 + floor(combo/4), cap 6? Score popup floats on canvas. Let me write it all now. Also handle mouse move over canvas for paddle, plus pointer lock not needed. Touch support. Keyboard arrows with velocity. Ball stuck to paddle before launch: state 'ready'. Draw ball on paddle top. Launch on click/space. States: 'menu','ready','play','paused','clear','dead','over','win'. Overlay screens in DOM with animated content. Let me also implement pause when window blurs. Right rail: score (big Bungee numerals), hi-score, combo chip, level, lives, progress bar, powerup log, mute toggle. Left rail: vertical "BLOCK BUSTER" text with Bungee rotated, plus a stylized brick stack, plus a coin slot detail. Now, guide section below with power-up cards (5) and tips + keyboard map. Scroll reveal with IntersectionObserver. Write compact but complete code. Canvas scaling: ``` function fit(){ const rect = wrap.getBoundingClientRect(); const dpr=Math.min(2,devicePixelRatio||1); canvas.width=W*dpr; canvas.height=H*dpr; ctx.setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0); } ``` CSS sets canvas width:100%, height:auto via aspect-ratio. Careful: setTransform each frame? Set once in fit. Then within draw, apply shake via ctx.save/translate. Fine. Let's write the brick drawing with cracks: draw base color, then if hp 5 with increasing speed. Let me now write the whole thing. I'll be thorough but efficient. Also add "HOLD" hint and "INSERT COIN" flavor. One more feature for "alive": animated brick pattern in ambient background, and a pulsing marquee, and the ball trail. Also add a subtle "ghost ball path" predictor? skip. Now code. For DOM overlays, I'll write a function `showOverlay(html)` and hide. Overlay screens: - menu: title, "PLAY", controls hint, hi-score - paused - level clear: name + bonus + "NEXT" auto after 1.6s or click - dead (life lost) - brief flash, no overlay, just flash + auto respawn ready. - gameover: score, stats, retry - win: after final level (level 8?) — I'll make endless so 'win' after clearing 8 levels: "ALL CLEAR". Let's cap at 8 levels (5 designed + 3 procedural) then win screen; but allow "CONTINUE" endless mode. Keep: after level 8, show victory with option to continue endless. Time tracking for bonus. Let me write the CSS now mentally with key pieces: ```css :root{ --ink:#0A0D16; --ink2:#111726; --line:#232C42; --bone:#F2EDE1; --verm:#FF4A2E; --amber:#FFC33D; --teal:#19C6AE; --mag:#FF3D8B; --steel:#4A5872; --font-display:'Bungee',sans-serif; --font-body:'Zen Kaku Gothic New',system-ui,sans-serif; } ``` Bungee only has 400.
